speechtext: It would, but I think that one-third is not an unfair . proposition. 1 think it is. an improvement over the pres ent condition. I believe it is based on some arrangement existing to-dav between the railway companies and certain of their employees. I think it is fair to the govern ment and not too severe upon the em plovee, and gives the government a certain measure of protection that seems desirable. '

It is quite proper that the immigration officers should be in uniform. But why adopt the principle in this department of paying two-thirds of the cost of the uniform and in another department paying the whole cost? If you are maintaining a principle in one case, it seems to me that you are stultifying yourself in another. If, for instance, the gov-enment says that customs officers must wear a uniform of a certain kind and quality which has to be paid for by the officers themselves, then I see no reason why the same thing should not apply here. If the government fix the duality _ and character of the uniform for officers^ in one branch-of the service, let them do the same thing in other branches of the service.
On the schedules,

If the minister would permit me, I would like to offer an amendment to section 2. I may be out of order, and if any one raises the question of order, I will not be able to do so. But I feel it my duty to suggest the following amendment to clause (i), and to insert after the word ' transport' in the thirteenth line, the words 'not including cattlemen'. My reason for doing so is that the Bill as now framed constitutes a cattleman, an immigrant. The steamship companies feel that it would oblige them perhaps to hold their vessel on some occasions ten or twelve hours in the city of Quebec. That delay might cause them to miss the tide, and if they missed the tide they might be detained 24 hours or 48 hours, and all that merely because there happened to be one

cattleman on that steamer. The steamship companies have sent a petition in asking the government not to make immigrants of cattlemen. The cattlemen themselves claim that they have a right to the privileges of Canadian citizenship, and should not be classed as immigrants. The Dominion Live Stock Association have passed resolutions asking that the government should not hamper their trade any more than is absolutely necessary. Unless the minister has some good reason that I do not know of, surely he will accept the amendment I am proposing. The fact of a man being a cattleman should not deprive him of his rights as a citizen. This does. The minister's Bill last session especially mentioned cattlemen but the present Bill does not. He gets over it ably by inserting the word 'transport'. The live stock trade is of such importance that it deserves the attention of the government and I hope the minister will agree to amend the Bill by inserting in the thirteenth line of section 2 after the word 'transport' the words 'including cattlemen'.
I do not see any special reason for that amendment to carry.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
speechtext: Last year we inserted the word 'cattlemen' in the section, and my hon. friend (Mr. Bickerdike) took very strong exception to this word being inserted, as placing the cattlemen in a class by themselves. This year we carefully omitted this word, and I am astonished to find him asking that this objectionable word be inserted in the Bill. Having met his views as expressed last session, I think in all fairness he should allow the Bill to remain in its present shape, and should not again raise the question of cattlemen. I agree that cattlemen are as good as other men, and this Bill treats them the same as other men. If cattlemen are Canadians or have acquired Canadian domicile they have the right to return to Canada. We make special provision in our interpretation for men who have been resident for three years in Canada, and, therefore, have acquired domicile. If a man is to all intents and purposes an immigrant, I cannot cenceive why he should be relieved from his position as an immigrant because he happens to have been employed in attendance on cattle.
Does the Bill not constitute cattlemen as being immigrants unless they have been in Canada three years?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
speechtext: Yes, certainly.
That is what I objected to, that does not apply to any other men.

* Mr. OLIVER. Every other man who has not been in Canada for three years is an immigrant. Why should not the cattleman be an immigrant the same as any *ther man?
Amendment negatived.
On the schedules,
There seems to be no form among the schedule for the certificate of the ship's physician as to the health of immigrants.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
speechtext:
Provision is made for that in section 73.
On section 45,

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
speechtext:
On looking over this section it seems to me that all interests will be served if the section were agreed to as amended.
Section as amended, agreed to.
Bill reported, read the third time, and passed. .

speechtext:
House went into committee to consider the following proposed resolution:
Resolved, that it is expedient to provide for the testing, marking, sale and use of glassware used in connection with the testing of milk, and to authorize the Governor in Council to make regulations with respect thereto, and for the imposition of penalties for offences in contravention thereof.

speakerposition: Minister of Agriculture
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GLASSWARE IN MILK TESTS.
speechtext: This resolution explains itself. There is a complaint that- these bottles are not correct sometimes, and that there is at present no means of securing their accuracy. In connection with the distribution of the money at cheese and butter factories, it is important to have them accurate.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GLASSWARE IN MILK TESTS.
speechtext: What kind of glassware will be included?

speakerposition: Minister of Agriculture
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GLASSWARE IN MILK TESTS.
speechtext:
The bottles that are used in what is known as the Babcock test for butter fat in milk.
Resolution reported, read the second time, and agreed to.
Mr. FISHER moved for leave to introduce Bill (No. 184) to provide for the testing of glassware used in connection with milk tests.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: Motion agreed to, and Bill read the first time.

speakerposition: topic
stagedirection
speechtext:
House went into committee to consider the following proposed resolution:

Resolved, that it is expedient to provide for the payment to members of the Commission for the Conservation of Natural Resources of their actual reasonable disbursements incurred in travelling to, returning from and remaining at meetings of the committees of the commission or attending to the business thereof.
What have been the expenses so far?

speakerposition: Minister of Agriculture
speechtext: Apart from the civil government vote, I think the only expense incurred has been that for the meeting held in Ottawa in January last.

I refer more particularly to the expense incurred by the government in connection with the establishing and carrying on of the work of the commission. I saw it announced that the chairman stated that he would make an application for $50,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Agriculture
speechtext: It is evident from the programme set out by the commission for the coming year that they would require a larger sum than is provided in the main estimates. The staff consists of a secretary in subdivision (a) of the first division; two officers in subdivisitn (b) of the first division, two in (b) of the second division, and two in (b) of the third division. There are some slight office expenses for stationery and printing. I will bring down the memorandum of the chairman of the commission on the second reading of the Bill.
Are these officers appointed by the commission?

speakerposition: Minister of Agriculture
speechtext:
They were appointed under the Civil Service Act, Mr. James White, geographer of the Interior Department was transferred to thi3 office, as I think was also one of the stenographers, and they are all appointed under the Civil Service Act.	.
Resolution reported, read the second time, and agreed to.
Mr. FISHER moved for leave to introduce Bill (No. 185) respecting the Commission for the Conservation of Natural Resources.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Motion agreed to, and Bill read the first time.

May I ask what will be the business to-morrow.

After that?

There are several resolutions-one in regard to the Montreal Harbour Commission, two Bills which stand in the name of the Postmaster General, the
Bills which have been introduced to-night, and several other Bills which are not likely to be of a contentious character.
